answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it can submit work or claim rewards. A bridge contract records the stake and links each claim to a verified task; if independent reviewers find duplicated or fabricated work, it forfeits the deposit. One attacker can still create an ocean of identities, but must fund each one, and detected fraud destroys that capital. A plume of cheap accounts therefore buys little influence unless it also carries real economic risk.
